mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 5% triggers a recessionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained high unemployment as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained industrial production decline as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below its 12-month moving average by more than 0.5% indicates deflationary pressure, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of deflationary CPIAUCSL moves as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE < 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of tight labor market conditions as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained GDPC1 growth as defined.
